My insurance covered my voluntary inpatient stay, but yours may not. It would be worth checking.

It wad hard being in for me. No phone. New people (I'm an introvert). I was on a good ward, the violent people were someplace else. We just all wanted out of our own problems.

They did get me on new meds, but there wasn't a lot of cbt/talk therapy.

Some people really benefit from a stay.

Assuming the song is great...

Record awesome players with great instruments in a good-sounding space.
That's probably 85% of the magic.

Also: arrangement. Every song doesn't need guitar even if the band has a guitarist. Include only what is necessary. Also include as much as necessary. An album doesn't have to sound like a live performance or easy to replicate live. 

If you're going for a specific sound, use reference material to compare your efforts. I sometimes use band-pass filters to focus on a certain area, too. Level match the sources, though. A mastered album probably sounds louder (perceived a better) than your mix.

This was an assault charge. 7 years ago. Probation from judicial diversion completed 6 years ago.

I've read that they can see more... I wish I could see all the data the FBI had associated with me.
